stops.name: Kutná Hora, the miners raise the Church of Saint Barbara
stops.campa: In the Bohemian silver town of Kutná Hora, whose entire wealth rises out of the veins its miners open in the rock, the miners' guild lays the first stones of a church to Barbara, patroness of subterranean work since the mountain once opened and closed around her, raising over decades a Gothic hall so vast and so ambitious it will not be finished for over five centuries. Frescoes inside will one day show the miners themselves at their work, offering their labor upward to the saint who tunneled into living stone and came out unharmed on the other side.

stops.name: Antwerp, Jan van Eyck draws Barbara before her unfinished tower
stops.campa: In the Low Countries the painter Jan van Eyck signs and dates a small panel of Saint Barbara seated in the foreground, reading, while behind her rises a tower still under construction, scaffolding and half-cut stone visible against the sky: the tower with three windows caught, uniquely in her whole iconographic tradition, in the act of being built rather than finished. The panel is left as a drawing under a thin grisaille wash, whether by design or interruption no one now can say, an unfinished image of an unfinished tower for a saint whose story is itself about a room completed against instruction.

stops.name: Vierzehnheiligen, the shepherd's vision, the fourteen children
stops.campa: Above the Cistercian abbey of Langheim in Franconia, the shepherd Hermann Leicht sees a crying child in the field and, stooping to lift it, watches it vanish; the vision returns weeks later with two burning candles beside it, and then, in June, a third time, bearing a red cross on its breast and surrounded by thirteen other children. We are the fourteen helpers, the child declares, and wish to erect a chapel here, where we can rest. Barbara stands among them as she has stood in Regensburg's prayers for a century, and the basilica that will one day rise on this field is named, simply, for the Fourteen.
stops.quote: We are the fourteen helpers, and wish to erect a chapel here, where we can rest. If you will be our servant, we will be yours.
stops.quote_source: The apparition to Hermann Leicht, June 1446, as preserved in the Langheim abbey tradition

stops.name: Segovia, the Real Colegio de Artillería names her patroness
stops.campa: In the Alcázar of Segovia, on the sixteenth of May, Lieutenant General Félix Gazola founds the Real Colegio de Artillería under Charles III, and the corps takes as its patroness the saint whose father was struck down by fire from the open sky: Barbara, invoked against the same thunder her tower's third window let in, now invoked for the controlled thunder of the gun. Every fourth of December the Academy keeps her feast as its own: cannon that answer to a name first spoken over a girl who converted her father's household gods into rubble before he ever raised a sword against her.

stops.name: Obernburg am Main, the Annakapelle and the verse of the three holy maids
stops.campa: Fifty kilometers up the Main from Frankfurt, in the little chapel of Saint Anne at Obernburg, a Nothelferaltar carved by Peter Vambach of Erlenbach sets Christ at the center of the Fourteen Helpers in four ranked rows, and beside it a plaque still carries the old rhyme of the three virgin sisters: Margaretha mit dem Wurm, Barbara mit dem Turm, Katharina mit dem Radl: those are the three holy maids. It is the same verse the essay's own accounting begins from, the mnemonic that keeps the tower-bearer bound in memory to the dragon-slayer and the wheel-breaker, three names that will not come apart.
stops.quote: Margaretha mit dem Wurm, Barbara mit dem Turm, Katharina mit dem Radl, das sind die drei heiligen Madl.
stops.quote_source: Plaque verse, Annakapelle, Obernburg am Main

stops.name: Madrid, the Museo Naval and the santabárbara of every Spanish ship
stops.campa: The Museo Naval opens in Madrid, gathering the models and relics of a navy whose every ship still calls its magazine of powder and shell by her name: the santabárbara, the compartment where the explosive heart of a warship is kept, named for the saint invoked against lightning and sudden detonation since her father was burned to ash on the mountain outside Heliopolis. In the museum's halls the models of the Santa Ana and the Santísima Trinidad carry, unmarked but understood by every sailor who served aboard them, a small stone room bearing a name that began as a tower with three windows.

stops.name: Weimar, the fourteen angels of the evening prayer
stops.campa: At the Deutsches Nationaltheater in Weimar, Richard Strauss conducts the premiere of Engelbert Humperdinck's Hänsel und Gretel, and the children of the opera sing their evening prayer into the lost forest: fourteen angels stand about me while I sleep. The line descends from the same Franconian devotion born at Langheim and carried down every German nursery since: Barbara's own company, numbered exactly, now watching over two children who, like her, are alone in a wood ruled by a hostile power. In this city of Goethe's own house the fourteen helpers step, briefly, out of chapel and into song.

stops.name: Domrémy, the Ladies' Tree, the third sister among the garlands
stops.campa: Under the great beech the country calls the Ladies' Tree, near the well Joffrey de Bourlémont built two hundred years before, the child Jehanne sings and dances with the other children of Domrémy and Greux, weaving garlands of flower and leaf for Our Lady and for whatever else still listens in that field. The trial record will keep only two of the three virgin martyrs at her side, Catherine and Margaret; but Katrin Vates's embroidery of this same hillside restores what the parchment dropped: Barbara, tower-bearer, third sister of the Heliopolitan triad, present at the tree with her sisters from the very beginning, the interpolation that fills a lacuna in a poem that rhymes.

stops.name: Domrémy, the tower over the field, the black window
stops.campa: On her own feast day, the fourth of December, the maiden of the tower keeps her appointment at the stone tower Joffrey de Bourlémont raised a lifetime before as a seat of grief and now finds turned to a house of annunciation. Joan climbs to it by night and communes there with Barbara, who teaches her the science of artillery and the opening of portals: the same rock-parting power that once carried a fleeing girl into a mountain in Heliopolis, now teaching a French girl how a black window opens in a wall, framed by lightning, and what it means to be one and the same with every maiden ever shut in a tower.

stops.name: Orléans, Les Tourelles, standing behind the Maid's cannon
stops.campa: Before the bridge-fort of the Tourelles, where the guns of the deliverance of Orléans speak all day into the English works and an arrow finds Jehanne above the breast exactly as she foretold it would, the gunners' saint stands unseen behind the Maid's own artillery, the tower-bearer who taught her the science of the cannon now present at the discharge of it, patroness of the thing she once suffered under a different name: fire that falls without warning and changes everything it touches. When the standard's tail brushes the wall and the fort falls in a rush, it is Barbara's ordnance as much as France's that has spoken.
